Case study: West Nashville, Tennessee

Source: vignettes/articles/nashville.Rmd
nashville.Rmd
Line TVA Maury–Davidson 500 kV, lattice towers, shared right-of-way (OSM way 19556523, 1.5–3.5 km from the Davidson end)
Setting Wooded hills, managed right-of-way
LiDAR TN_DavidsonCounty_D22, Tennessee State Plane US survey feet, ~34 pts/m², with vendor vegetation (3–5) and building (6) classes
Line length, above-ground points 2.0 km, 1.05 M
Conductor returns found 104,181, along ~100% of the line
Result Decisive: no grow-in, 24 strike trees in 7 segments, 32 clear
Nashville risk map

The conductor is measured along the whole line

Nashville conductor profile

The 500 kV bundles were well sampled: 104,181 conductor returns, three phases at about −12, 0 and +12 m, and a second circuit sharing the right-of-way at +30–45 m. The profile shows clean catenaries between towers, about 15–45 m above the ground (median 24 m).

Nashville cross-section

Wires transfer across space here; the Colorado model does not

Classifier against weak labels (spatial blocks):

class n prevalence avg. precision, spatial blocks random folds spatial, no height/echo
wire 104,181 0.10 0.91 0.94 0.86
structure 4,262 0.004 0.008 0.26 0.006
Nashville cross-validation

Wires transfer across space here: average precision 0.91 against a no-skill 0.10, and 0.86 even without the height and echo features, the most direct proxies for the labelling rule. Structures (31 lattice towers) still don’t.

Against the vendor’s classes. These are independent of the weak labels. A geometric conductor zone (inside the measured conductor envelope, within 3 m of the conductor or above) is excluded from scoring for every method alike, because the vendor put conductors in vegetation. Vegetation is 98.5% of the scored points, so its F1 can’t show skill: predicting “vegetation” everywhere scores 0.992.

vegetation F1 building F1 balanced accuracy Cohen’s κ
always “vegetation” (baseline) 0.992 0 0.50 0
weak labels 0.950 0 0.46 0.07
model trained on weak labels 0.957 0 0.47 −0.01
Colorado model, transferred 0.992 0 0.50 0.00
trained on vendor labels (spatial CV) 0.998 0.87 (AP 0.95) 0.89 —
  • On vegetation vs building, the weak-label pipeline has no skill at this site. OSM maps one building in the corridor, so there are no building labels to learn from. The vendor’s labels would buy a building F1 of 0.87. The weak models’ lower vegetation recall is mostly second-circuit conductors and abstentions, which the vendor also calls vegetation.
  • The Colorado model doesn’t transfer. With its own class prior it recalls 0% of Nashville’s conductor returns. Threshold-free, its wire average precision is 0.20 against a 0.10 baseline (the Nashville model: 0.86). Its 0.992 vegetation F1 is exactly the baseline.

Vendor vegetation classes contain the conductors

99.3% of the conductor returns (103,449 points, 15–45 m up) are delivered as high vegetation. The same segments, screened with three different canopy models:

canopy model grow-in fall-in clear
vendor vegetation classes, as delivered 39 0 0
vendor vegetation + this package’s conductor removal 0 10 29
this package (consensus vegetation + conductor removal) 0 7 32
  • The delivered classes would send crews to every span. Removing conductor returns is the whole grow-in correction (39 → 0). Consensus labelling (model and weak rules agreeing on vegetation, vendor buildings removed) then trims fall-in from 10 segments to 7.
  • No grow-in. The managed right-of-way is clear under the conductors.
  • The 32 clear segments were seen, not assumed. Every segment has at least 91% of its corridor and of its grow-in zone observed (median 99%), so none is tiered no data. The lowest segment (0.36–0.41 km, 91% under the line) is still 16 points above the 75% threshold.
  • 24 strike trees across 7 segments, 28–39 m from the centreline, the same under both bounds because the conductor is measured. They are the list to verify.
  • The conductor envelope has to cover every phase. An earlier run capped it at 15 m while one outer phase sits up to ~19 m from the OSM centreline. That left outer-phase returns in the canopy model, which showed up as 2 grow-in segments and 4 extra strike trees at the envelope edge. Widening the grow-in zone to 21 m removed all of them.

Configuration 

run_case_study(list(
  id = "nashville",
  line_ids = "19556523", window_m = c(1500, 3500), start_north = TRUE,
  project = "TN_DavidsonCounty_D22",
  tiles = sprintf("USGS_LPC_TN_DavidsonCounty_D22_%s.laz",
                  c("155020", "155060", "155100", "155140", "169020")),
  half_width_m = 60, wire_search_m = 20, phase_offset_m = 11,
  under_line_m = 21, wire_zone_m = 25, structure_mask_m = 18,
  min_ground_clear_m = 8.5,            # NESC 232-1 order of magnitude for 500 kV
  attach_m = 45,                       # upper limit on lattice attachment height
  vendor_classes = TRUE,
  transfer_from = "sunshine"           # score the Colorado model here
))

The full script is analysis/run_nashville.R.
